- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and price is near mean, model often predicts mean reversion too aggressively; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is rising (0.3–0.5) and price is rising, model often overestimates; apply 1–2% downward correction for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low and price is near recent low; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid missing bottom.
